title: mainnet-addresses.ts comments describe three REAL non-zero mainnet addresses as "not yet deployed / zero placeholders", inverting exactly the distinction the mainnet port depends on
description: The comments at :136 and :142 read 'NudgeRatchet dispatcher + its mint-debt hook — not yet deployed on mainnet (story 068). Zero placeholders so this file still satisfies the ContractAddresses interface' and 'Dedicated NFTStaker … not yet deployed on mainnet (story 068)'. The values beneath them are real, non-zero, deployed mainnet addresses: NudgeRatchet 0xd4ea91f6096A75a1c34A3c25D7725dE1f5c49f68, NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook 0x09AceB96337df1316e0D2d7EEEa44d754D1f8d05, RatchetNFTStaker 0x299b0071def42d35eaf5ea24cc0a71cf10655a64, RatchetBatchNFTMinter 0x81896f48a95abea255cd38a3010e985b6051a1c7.
impact: Seventy lines above, two entries in the SAME file genuinely are zero placeholders (DEV-06). An operator reading this file to decide what still needs deploying gets the answer exactly backwards for four entries. Given the stated next step is a hand-written differential mainnet script that must source live addresses from this file and distinguish deployed from not-deployed, this is the single most decision-relevant piece of misinformation in the address book. It is also a Law-3 footgun: the comment is the artifact a competent operator would trust.
attackPath: No attack path. The comments at :136 and :142 state 'not yet deployed on mainnet (story 068). Zero placeholders...' above four real, non-zero, deployed mainnet addresses: NudgeRatchet 0xd4ea91f6..., NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook 0x09AceB96..., RatchetNFTStaker 0x299b0071..., RatchetBatchNFTMinter 0x81896f48...
evidence: Direct read of server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:136-145. Corroborated by package.json's `//fix-ratchet-sink` doc comment, which describes live owner-only operations against the NudgeRatchet and RatchetBatchNFTMinter — i.e. contracts that are demonstrably deployed and in production use.
recommendation: Correct the four comments to record the actual deployment dates and the story that shipped them. Adopt a single, machine-checkable convention for 'not yet deployed' (see DEV-06) so a comment can never contradict a value. Consider a lint/CI check asserting that any entry commented 'not yet deployed' holds address(0) and vice versa.

classification.likelihood: Decision-relevance is high; realised harm requires a multi-step operator sequence that chain state would contradict at several points.
classification.assumptions: Non-malicious operator hand-writing the differential mainnet script and reading this file to decide what still needs deploying.
classification.externalRequirements: The operator must trust the prose over on-chain state AND complete a re-deploy and sink re-point without noticing the fresh contract has no state.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal. C4 places comment defects in QA/Low by name, and I am holding that line conservatively (rule 4: when uncertain, classify lower). The escalation argument was considered and rejected: to reach Medium the operator would have to believe the prose over chain state and carry a full re-deploy plus sink re-point of an already-live NudgeRatchet / RatchetBatchNFTMinter to completion without the freshly-deployed, state-less contract giving it away. That is exactly the hand-wavy multi-step hypothetical the High/Medium bar excludes. It is nonetheless the FIX-FIRST item among the Lows, for two reasons. First, decision-relevance: the stated next step is a hand-written differential mainnet script that must read this exact file to distinguish deployed from not-deployed, and seventy lines above, two entries in the SAME file genuinely ARE zero placeholders (DEV-06) - so the operator gets the answer exactly backwards for four entries while getting it right for two, which is worse than uniformly wrong. Second, the repo's standing principle that in-source documentation carries no suppression authority and that falsely-confident prose RAISES rather than lowers weight applies squarely: the comment is the artifact a competent operator would trust. Corroborated by package.json's `//fix-ratchet-sink` doc comment, which describes live owner-only operations against contracts this file calls undeployed. Recommend the machine-checkable remedy (CI assertion that any entry commented 'not yet deployed' holds address(0), and vice versa) rather than a prose correction, so the two findings are fixed by one control.
severityAgreement: AGREE with proposed low - but flagged as the FIX-FIRST Low of this set

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
